title: Batching & Prefix Cache: Latency-Quality Regression Evaluation and Rollout Plan
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Objective:
Run an end-to-end evaluation that quantifies the latency vs. generation-quality tradeoffs introduced by proposed batching and prefix/KV cache configuration changes. Use the eval harness and production-like traffic mixes to determine safe canary thresholds and an automated rollback policy.

Scope and goals:
- Evaluate combinations of (batch_size: 1,4,8,16), (max_batch_latency_ms: 5,10,25), and (prefix_cache_ttl_s: 0,30,300) across two model variants (ggml-0616 and open-rw-13b-quant).
- Measure latency distribution (p50, p95, p99), token-level cost, throughput, and quality regressions using the canonical eval suite (QA accuracy, instruction-following F1, hallucination rate) and a curated set of customer prompts.
- Produce a decision matrix that maps config tuples -> recommended rollout strategy (canary %, fallback model, per-route override).

Success criteria / gates:
- Any config must keep request-p95 <= baseline_p95 + 25ms for latency-sensitive routes (chat-short).
- Overall eval-suite accuracy drop must be <= 0.5% absolute versus pinned model baseline. If drop is between 0.5% and 1.5%, require manual review and staged rollout with extended monitoring. >1.5% = reject.
- Cost per token reduction target: >=10% for batch/caching combos without violating the above guards.

Methodology:
1) Synthetic load: replay production sampled traces (session length distribution, seq lengths) on a dedicated canary infra to separate infra noise from config effect.
2) Eval harness: run batch of 5k labelled prompts covering edge instructions, long-context generation, and contextual retrieval cases. Compute per-prompt delta metrics and aggregate with confidence intervals.
3) Observability: capture per-request model variant, batch_size, cache_hit boolean, kv_cache_keys, token counts, and embed into eval dashboard. Add regression alerts tied to eval-suite thresholds.
4) Human review: triage any prompt groups with >3% relative drop for qualitative analysis and write short remediation notes (prompt tweaks, cache exclusions).

Test matrix and priority routes:
- Priority A: chat-short, code-completion (latency-sensitive).
- Priority B: longform generation, summarization (throughput-sensitive).

Rollout plan:
- Start with internal canary using canary-flag + dataset replay.
- If gates pass: 1% customer canary for 24h (auto-metrics monitoring).
- Expand to 10% for 48h then 50% for 72h. On any triggered regression alert revert to previous config and open a postmortem.
- Provide route-level opt-out flag for customers that require strict latency/quality profiles.

Notes about trade-offs:
- Larger batch sizes yield 18-30% token-cost reduction in our microbenchmarks but increase p95 by ~20-45ms depending on kernel queueing.
- Prefix caching reduces repeated context tokens for retrieval-heavy flows, but can surface stale context for dynamic prompt inputs (risk manifest in instruction-following tests).
- For quantized models, batching interacts with kernel choices and occasionally increases variance in generation timing; include per-kernel monitoring.

Deliverables:
- Eval report PDF with decision matrix and recommended rollout configs.
- Github PR(s) implementing feature-flagged runtime changes + unit/integration tests.
- Dashboard panels (p99 latency by route, eval-suite delta heatmap, cache-hit impact view).
- Canary rollout runbook and automated rollback actions.
